correctness.rationale: The arbitrary-n proof uses an exhaustive classification of permutations at inversion length two, pairwise-intersecting two-element sets, and strict equality in both parity slices. A separate contradiction eliminates center distance 3 or greater. Neighborhood-center uniqueness identifies one anticode with exactly one permutohedron edge; elementary orbit counting finishes. The finite checker reconstructs every n=5 and n=6 Kendall distance with independent inversion and shortest-path algorithms, exhaustively enumerates maximal anticodes and double balls, verifies the group orbits, and checks local inversion patterns through n=7. Finite data are not used to justify the universal bound.

originality.rationale: The 2014 source Theorem 7 and 2015 full-length source Theorem 8 establish the sharp 2(n-1) maximum and exhibit adjacent-center double balls. They do not classify all equality cases, prove uniqueness of centers, count n!(n-1)/2 labeled maxima or derive the n-dependent orbit partition. The new parity-class equality lemma supplies the missing strict implication. Searches for diameter-three anticode equality, double-ball uniqueness, Kendall anticodes and their code-anticode aliases found no stronger covering statement. Originality is qualified by the residual risk of an unindexed equivalent proof.
residual_risks: The all-extremizer classification could occur in an obscure or unindexed later work absent from the targeted searches.
The small length n=4 lies outside the theorem and admits exceptional parity-slice behavior.
The orbit result is for the specified explicit isometry subgroup; no classification under hypothetical extra isometries is claimed.

value.rationale: This is a natural infinite-family equality classification at the canonical first odd anticode diameter in Kendall rank-modulation coding. Unlike the known bound and one sharp construction, rigidity identifies every extremal configuration with a unique permutohedron edge, computes its exact labeled count for all n, and distinguishes all positional symmetry types including the central even-n exceptional stabilizer. These are structurally motivated properties relevant to diameter-perfect/code-anticode methods, not a routine restatement of the optimum size.
